title: kv-striped-reservoir-evictor-and-spill-hedging-for-reduced-fragmentation
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: Long-running tenant workloads observed pathological KV cache fragmentation during mixed short/long context traffic. This PR introduces a striped reservoir allocator plus an eviction gate and spill-hedging policy that reduces tail evictions and spill churn. Key goals: 1) reduce fragmentation by avoiding cross-stripe allocation for long-lived KV entries; 2) smooth spill bursts by hedging small background writes and coordinating with pager; 3) preserve latency SLOs under heavy continuous-batching loads.

What changed (high level): Implemented a striped-reservoir allocator that shards the KV arena by lifetime/size buckets; a lightweight eviction gate that defers low-priority evictions for a short adaptive window; a spill hedging algorithm that aggregates candidate spill writes and issues prioritized batch spills to the pager. Also touches kernel selection hints and scheduler backpressure hooks so eviction decisions respect active compute batching windows. Added metrics and traces for fragment score, stripe occupancy, spill batch sizes, and eviction gate hold times.

Checklist: [x] Implementation and unit tests for allocator & evictor [x] Integration tests with pager simulator [x] Benchmarks (micro + canary) [x] Docs: design note and metrics mapping [ ] Follow-up: tenant-level tuning UI in Console (ENG-8472).
commits_summary: 5 commits: initial striped reservoir scaffolding; stripe selection policy; eviction-gate core logic; spill hedging and pager integration; metrics + tests + docs.
diff_snippets: striped_reservoir.cpp: added stripe selection loop with lifetime histogram sampling; eviction_gate.cpp: new adaptive-window timer and priority buckets; spill_hedger.cpp: batch coalescer + pager client priority tags; runtime scheduler: register eviction hold callback to avoid preempting active batching windows.
tests_run: unit (kv allocator/evictor) passed; integration (pager sim) passed; microbench: median latency unchanged, p99 latency improved ~12% under mixed load; end-to-end canary on perf cluster showed 8% lower spill bytes/hour and 15% fewer eviction events.
review_comments: Liam O'Connor: 'Can you explain how stripe sizing adapts to multi-tenant skew? Need to avoid a tenant hogging a stripe.'
Ava Martinez: 'Stripe sizing uses a periodic rebalancer that samples tenant residency; we added tenant-aware min/max caps to avoid hijacking.'
Priya Singh: 'Eviction gate hold time seems like it could increase memory pressure in worst-case; add guardrails.'
Ava Martinez: 'Added two guardrails: hard eviction deadlines per stripe and reactive bypass if usable memory < 6%.'
Marcus Lee: 'Pager integration looks good, but ensure we preserve ordering for writeback to avoid double-writes.'
Ava Martinez: 'Spill hedger tags original sequence ids; pager client enforces per-tenant ordering before finalizing.'
Marcus Lee: 'CI flake on integration; re-run resolved it.'
ci_summary: CI initially failed on an unrelated lint rule; fixed style in stripe header and re-ran. Unit and integration tests then passed. Performance benchmark job passed on second run. All checks green.
release_notes: kv: introduce striped reservoir allocator and eviction gate to reduce KV cache fragmentation and spill churn; spill hedging reduces paging bursts and improves p99 latency under mixed workloads. No user-facing API changes. Tenant tuning flags added for ops teams.
manual_steps: Ops: enable feature flag 'kv.striped_reservoir' in clusters to opt-in; default is off until gradual rollout. Requires matching pager minor version >= 0.19.2.
observability: New metrics: kv.stripe.occupancy, kv.fragment_score, kv.eviction_gate_hold_ms, kv.spill_hedge_batch_size. Added traces on eviction path (span:kv.evict).
performance_notes: Bench details: simulated 100 tenants with mixed short (<=64 token) and long (>=2048 token) sessions; continuous batching enabled. Observed 12% p99 improvement and 8% decrease in spill bytes/hour during steady-state. Memory overhead ~0.6% due to stripe metadata.
